acts.name: Promise: cold open, science, origin, rules, childhood perks
Ally and price: Milo, problems 1-4, identity cost
Want: Milo taken, year-long search, infiltration, the folder
Set piece: stadium mission, betrayal-by-disguise, chase fight
Truth: sibling reveal, accusation, cliffhanger, CTA

loops.what: Your disguises always speak in a little kid's voice -> you finally do her voice perfectly at the decisive moment
Dog barks only at you -> Problem 2: smell can't be faked
Rule 1 you keep your weight -> goalpost survives the flyer; 'weighs like a whole person'; gravity beaten by going flat
Rule 2 you can only become what you studied -> 30 days studying the gray-coat woman from inside the case
Photo of yourself in your pocket -> you turn back into you on the field
Gray gloves on the van driver -> she stops wearing gloves; bare hands on the wheel
Peanut-butter granola bars -> Jay's last question to you
Milo's folder marked 'Found' -> 'ask her' -> her face closes when you say his name
Who really drives the black vans? Is she telling the truth?

beats.summary: Two identical moms in the kitchen; dad runs an identity test; the fake mom answers in a small boy's voice; the dog barks only at you; real mom sends you to your room.
Title question, widened to 'anyone or anything', then the mechanism pivot.
visual: title card over hallway transformation shimmer

beats.summary: Teaser, then a real animal that already does a version: skin colour and pattern change in under a second; twist: the animal is likely colourblind.
How it feels: bones slide, face folds, hair retracts; three seconds; like a morning stretch.
People know thousands of faces and have brain hardware for them, so a familiar face fools anyone; the world becomes a costume shop.

Discovery at age six during hide-and-seek: you wish yourself into a laundry basket, win, then can't stand up for an hour. Socks dumped on you; you pop back and your mom screams, then sits down on the floor.
Nightly practice. Rule 1: you keep your full body weight, so a house cat version weighs a dozen cats and breaks the couch.
Rule 2: you only become what you have studied; the teacher copy is perfect from the front and wrong from the back.
Rule 3: you get the look but not the skill; voice is hardest, so for years every disguise talks like a little kid.

Childhood montage: unbeatable at hide-and-seek (coat rack, plant, Christmas tree), forging a permission slip, a fake principal announcement that collides with the real principal, a too-heavy zoo penguin.
Best friend Milo, the only one who knows, has his own secret: he talks to animals (a crow once found someone's keys). Mutual admiration exchange.
Problem 1, weight again: small forms are dense; a mouse that weighs as much as a big dog; a bird that can never fly. Milo translates the pigeons' complaint.
Problem 2, dogs: noses with fifty times your smell sensors know who you are whatever face you wear.
Problem 3, details: fingerprints, scars and habits can't be copied; dad's phone politely refuses you. Theme line: the outside is easy, the inside is hard.

Problem 4, the one nobody warned you about: after weeks as someone else you can't rebuild your own face; mom notices; old school photos fix it. You carry a photo of yourself from now on. Rule 4 stated.
Keeping it small works, until Milo's bird stunt goes viral. Narrator reminds you what happens to powered kids on the news. Days later a black van takes Milo; he doesn't resist.
visual: 3D street black van, men in dark jackets

beats.summary: Clue: the driver's gray gloves. You chase on a bike and lose it. Adults give cover stories; pigeons wait. You state the goal out loud.
A year as a hundred people: mail carrier, desk officer, old man with pigeons (useless). Rumours from another episode lead to a gray coat and a gray van; three grays line up.
visual: 3D gym collapse flashback with floating crowd

beats.summary: Two weeks to find the van; a garage behind a car wash. A mind-reader rules out walking in as a person, so you become an equipment case in the corner for a month.

Life as furniture: the team's small kindnesses and habits, a teleporter who grabs a snack beside you daily, a near-miss with the mind-reader that forces you to stop thinking for hours. Worst part: they're nice.

Midpoint reveal: the leader returns alone, gloves gone, makes a guilty phone call about a promise. You pick her locked drawer: dossiers on every team kid with how to stop them, and Milo's folder marked with one word.

Alarm: the two villains are at a 70,000-seat championship game, where a touch-copier can harvest powers by shaking hands. You're carried to the van as the case (too heavy). Team recaps the last failure and vows no touching; the leader's bare hands on the wheel.

The stadium is already frozen: ball mid-spiral, fireworks pressed in the sky, 70,000 still people; the team freezes as it exits. Only the gray-coat woman moves, walking toward the boy holding time while her brother touches spectators.
She cuffs the time-stopper to a goalpost; time crashes back. Each team member lands one move from their own episode; the copier is pinned. A sibling reveal in one line.
visual: 3D stadium action: webs, gravity glow, teleport blink

beats.summary: 'For one second it really is over', then the case opens. You become the leader, perfectly including the voice, and order the team to let go. Two identical leaders face off; the team is frozen by doubt.
Doubt gives the copier his opening: he steals the strong kid's power by touch. You free the time-stopper with a hand shaped like the key you watched for a month.

Chase fight as a chain of rule payoffs: you copy the teleporter, slip a web, become a goalpost the flyer bounces off, a jersey pile, a tiger mascot; the gravity kid crushes you, so you go flat as a tarp using a science-class principle.
The villains run; the strong kid is weakened; the leader catches her brother at the tunnel. Time stops again, and both siblings still move.
He copied time-stopping from her long ago. He gently frees himself, kneels by the tarp, and tells you to ask her who drives the vans.
They vanish; touched spectators stare at their hands. You turn back using your pocket photo. The team circles you; two running gags land, then nobody laughs. The leader studies your face.

You say Milo's name; something closes in her face. You repeat the accusation; the whole team turns. She says nothing, takes out the keys you studied, orders everyone into the van, including you, and won't meet their eyes.
Three questions: what would you do; hide or walk in as yourself; is she telling the truth. Sign-off.
